articles.title: Ceferin brands Infantino’s failed World Cup plan as ‘even worse than the Super League’
articles.summary: Fifa president will face opponent if he seeks re-election. Ceferin: ‘We stopped another try to steal the sport’ The Uefa president, Aleksander Ceferin, has described Gianni Infantino’s doomed attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup as “even worse than the Super League plan” and warned his embattled…
body: Ceferin has led Uefa’s firm collective stance against the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme, which was shelved amid widespread opposition at the start of August. Uefa are pushing for Infantino to quit, also drawing on support from Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, and are yet to drop a threat to boycott Fifa competitions while talks are under way with Concacaf to set up a combined Nations League tournament.

In an interview with the podcast The Rest is Politics: Leading, Ceferin denounced Infantino’s project as more damaging than the breakaway Super League that was shelved in 2021 after large-scale protests. “I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan,” he said. “In the first case, super-important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

“I’m absolutely sure that the [FFE] plan is dead. For me, the most important thing is that we stopped another try to sell the sport. It’s hard to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone.”
points: Fifa president will face opponent if he seeks re-election.

articles.title: Arthur Fils wins first Masters title after beating Frances Tiafoe in Cincinnati final
articles.summary: 22-year-old wins 6-3, 1-6, 6-0. Fils now ranked No 11 in world. Arthur Fils has always believed he was on the path to the very top of his chosen sport. Even when others considered him too young, too green or far too self-confident, he has entered the biggest tournaments in the world with the…
body: On a historic afternoon in Mason, Ohio, Fils took an huge step forward in pursuit of those massive goals as the 22-year-old became a Masters 1000 champion for the first time in his young career. His greatest achievement was secured with a supreme mental effort under pressure as the Frenchman dragged himself back into contention after a desperate second set, recovering to defeat Frances Tiafoe 6-3, 1-6, 6-0 and win the Cincinnati Open.

Even before a ball was struck, this was a historic moment: the first ATP Masters 1000 final played between two black players. The pair have built such a great rapport that before this match, the biggest final of their careers, they cracked jokes together as they departed the practice courts side-by-side. After taking a customary picture with the guest invited on-court to deliver the coin toss, Fils insisted on taking a picture with Tiafoe alone to mark the occasion.

articles.title: Start your engines! Trump completes fast and furious takeover of Washington with IndyCar race
articles.summary: US president, pushing on with Freedom 250 festivities, makes over nation’s capital for Trump rally on wheels. Kyle Kirkwood wins Freedom 250 IndyCar race after Trump waves the green flag. He got the wrong end of the stick.
body: H e got the wrong end of the stick. Donald Trump couldn’t figure out how to hold the green flag until his wife, Melania Trump, and Command Sgt Maj Matt Williams set him right. Then the US president waved the flag fast and furious like an excited schoolboy. The race was under way – and his conquest of Washington DC was complete.

Since returning to Washington, Trump has deployed the national guard, wrecked the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool, demolished the East Wing of the White House and run the John F Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts into the ground. His face adorns the Department of Justice, and he still has grand plans for a triumphal arch worthy of a Roman emperor.

On Sunday he made the nation’s capital tremble with fast, flashy cars brazenly roaring around a 1.7-mile street circuit in IndyCar’s Freedom ⁠250 Grand Prix, the capstone of his Maga-flavoured celebration of the 250th anniversary of US independence.

articles.title: Infantino must remember he is European - Ceferin
articles.summary: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin says his Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino's attempt to sell off a stake in the World Cup was "worse than the Super League".
body: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin says Gianni Infantino needs to remember he is European after describing his Fifa counterpart's plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup as "worse than the Super League".

Earlier this month the world governing body abandoned Infantino's proposal to create a new company - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) - to manage the commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, with 21% to be sold off to a private investment company.
Uefa led opposition to the plan, with its members voting to boycott World Cups unless it was scrapped.
European football's governing body has since said it has lost confidence in Infantino, while the football associations of all the home nations have withdrawn support for the 56-year-old Swiss.

articles.title: How Hull kept plan to stun Man Utd secret
articles.summary: Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic kept his plan to topple Manchester United on their Premier League return under wraps for weeks, assistant head coach Dean Holden tells Match of the Day.
body: The Tigers produced a sensational 2-0 opening-weekend win over Michael Carrick's side on Saturday while deploying a back five.
Hull were making their first Premier League appearance in nine years after coming up through the play-offs last year.
First-half goals from defenders Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy gave them their first league win over United since 1974.

Jakirovic altered his tactics for the game, having watched a couple of United's pre-season matches, including the 4-2 defeat by AC Milan, engineered by former boss Ruben Amorim, when he repeatedly switched play to his wing-backs, which United's defence failed to cover.

articles.title: Is there a loophole in judge’s ruling that is allowing NFL players to return to college football?
articles.summary: On Sunday, the college football world officially entered uncharted territory when the Cleveland Browns waived Dae’Quan Wright. If Wright goes unclaimed, he will be free to sign with a college football team, most likely the LSU Tigers.
body: Wright went through the NFL Draft process, went undrafted, and was actively participating in the preseason before entering the transfer portal. According to CBS Sports, he won’t be the only player to do so. This could be possible because of a minor detail in the judge’s ruling.

“Despite [Judge] Sweeney clarifying on Aug. 2 that NCAA rules would still apply regarding players who’ve signed NFL contracts and are ineligible to return to college, teams have remained in contact with different players about a potential return to school, sources told CBS Sports,” Brad Crawford of CBS Sports reported.

“This Louisiana TRO has created a time-sensitive window for players who are in NFL training camps or on the cut bubble. NFL teams will trim their final rosters to 53 players on Aug. 30, which could create opportunities for released players to play college football during the 2026 season on a NIL or revenue share contract.”

articles.title: Four competitive-match debuts at BVB: These new signings have us wanting more
articles.summary: Even for BVB head coach Niko Kovac, it quickly became clear despite the 1-2 loss to Bayern: “All four showed why we signed them.”Joane Gadou completed the entire preseason and established himself...
body: Giannis Konstantelias likely made the biggest impression on Saturday evening. The Greek player joined training for the first time on Friday but was still given the opportunity to play against Bayern Munich starting in the 46th minute.

Surprisingly, the 23-year-old needed no time to find his rhythm. As early as the 52nd minute, he attempted a spectacular bicycle kick that was narrowly blocked. Even after that, he was directly involved in many counterattacks and scoring chances. This included the 1-2 goal by Fabio Silva, which Konstantelias set up with a very fine pass. Niko Kovac praised him highly: “He did really well. The way he set up that goal was top-notch.”
With his creativity and drive forward, Konstantelias should quickly earn himself even more playing time.
Joey Veerman, too, has only had a few training sessions with his new team under his belt. He made his BVB debut in the 62nd minute.

articles.title: Is Fils favourite to win US Open? Frenchman beats Tiafoe to win Cincinnati title
articles.summary: Frenchman Arthur Fils may have played himself into contention to win the US Open after sealing the biggest title of his career at the Cincinnati Open on Sunday.
body: The 21st seed, who won the Barcelona Open in April, added the Cincy crown to his growing list of achievements with a topsy-turvy 6-3 1-6 6-0 victory over Frances Tiafoe in Ohio.
Fils became the third Black man to win a Masters 1000 title, joining Ben Shelton, who won the Canadian Open twice, and Jo-Wilfried Tsonga, who won Paris in 2008 and Canada in 2014.

articles.title: Houston coach Ralph Sampson: Chris Cenac Jr. will be a 3-point shooter with Boston Celtics
articles.summary: The Boston Celtics have had great success developing big men in recent years (look no further to Neemias Queta for their latest example). And have thrived when they have had a center able to shoot the ball, with vets like Al Horford to Kristaps Porzingis the most recent examples.
body: This tendency has not been lost on Ralph Sampson, the college coach of new Boston big man Chris Cenac Jr., the former of which recently shared his perspective on why the Celtics could be an ideal team for the former University of Houston center to grow his game as a pro. "There's a reason why the best organizations have the best cultures, because things like that matter," said Sampson in a recent interview with Boston Globe reporter Adam Himmelsbach.

"Little things like that are big things when it comes to work ethic and getting better," he continued. "I don't know that (Payton) Pritchard would be a great player everywhere, but he made it in Boston, and I don't think it was a coincidence that it was in Boston."

" Jayson Tatum is going to be good everywhere, but some of those other guys might not be," he added. "I think Chris can develop there... Chris is going to be a 37-39 percent shooter (from 3). He's got a great release, and the ball comes off his fingertips with a good rotation and a good arc, and he's a worker. He's not like a guard who has been shooting 3s his whole life."

articles.title: Atlanta Braves Announce Sudden Drake Baldwin Decision During Brewers Series
articles.summary: The Atlanta Braves desperately need a victory after losing seven of their last nine games, including each of the first two games of their series against the Milwaukee Brewers.
body: On Sunday, Atlanta will face Milwaukee one more time in the series finale at Journey Bank Ballpark at Historic Bowman Field in Williamsport, Pennsylvania, as part of the Little League Classic.
Ahead of the game, however, Braves manager Walt Weiss made a sudden lineup change involving All-Star catcher Drake Baldwin.
Baldwin has spent most of the season near the top of the order, batting either leadoff or directly behind Ronald Acuna Jr. in the No. 2 spot.
On Sunday, Weiss has moved Baldwin all the way down to the No. 5 spot, marking the first time this season that he has batted there.

articles.title: Late Clark magic holds off McIlroy and Cantlay in PGA Tour thriller
articles.summary: Wyndham Clark overcame blowing a five-shot lead to edge out Rory McIlroy with a dramatic three-shot victory at the PGA Tour's BMW Championship.
body: Clark saw his big overnight lead disappear during a thrilling Sunday at Bellerive Country Club, where the US Open champion bogeyed three of his first 10 holes to give hope to McIlroy and the chasing pack.

McIlroy found three birdies in a four-hole stretch around the turn to sit level with Clark heading into the closing stretch, only for his playing partner to post a three-birdie finish to cap off a roller-coaster victory in style.

A level-par 70 was enough for Clark to end the week on 17 under and close out a third PGA Tour victory of the season, following on from the CJ Cup Byron Nelson and the US Open, with Patrick Cantlay claiming solo second to progress through to next week's season-ending Tour Championship.

McIlroy was tied for the lead with three to play but ended four back after a penultimate-hole bogey and Clark's impressive birdie burst, while Gary Woodland, Collin Morikawa and Chris Gotterup shared fourth place.
